scene_refinement.what: rotation_matrix corrected on real footage so the two cameras agree for a scene at infinity. Only parallax-free measurements were used, so nothing that depends on where the rig stands went into the calibration; parallax is left to --shift-top/--shift-bottom.

how.pitch: vertical offset at the seam column (no parallax there: the baseline is perpendicular to that view direction)
how.roll: left-to-right change of the vertical offset across the overlap, fitted as constant + a parallax term growing with tan^2(angle below horizon); only the constant part was absorbed
how.yaw: horizontal offset on the far field just below the horizon (parallax ~0 at any baseline)
how.axes: pitch about the horizontal axis at the seam, roll about the seam view direction, yaw about the canvas vertical (cam0 frame), applied as R = R_board * Rp * Rr * Ry

scene_refinement.measured_on: take_20261003_133914 frames 0 and 3000 (rig ~15-18 ft up). After: vertical offset ~0.3 px, far-field horizontal ~0; that scene then needs shift-top -3 / shift-bottom +8.4 (pure parallax).
scene_refinement.not_absorbed: translation_mm is still the board solve (its 4.6 mm vertical component is a solve artifact; the stitcher ignores translation). Horizontal parallax measures ~1/3 of what a 68 mm baseline predicts, likely lens-model (intrinsics) error at the fisheye edges; not a rotation, so left to the shear.
